points.text: Human preference comparison unfair to Masquerade because Mitty uses human-in-the-loop filtering.
Quality of synthetic paired data and its downstream effects questioned.
No real-robot experiments or actions; unclear whether good videos yield accurate actions.
Model novelty incremental: Wan 2.2 with LoRA and bidirectional attention.
Synthetic data pipeline may introduce domain bias and accumulated errors.
No quantitative real-world task success metrics.
Task is essentially video-to-video translation specialized to robotics.
No evidence that generated videos are useful for robotics.
Improper citation spacing.
Mixed-training benefit claim contradicted by Table 2; text sections disagree.
No ablation with versus without synthetic EPIC data.
No matched-data baseline using intermediate representations or other conditioning.
Human2Robot, a directly related method, not compared.
Cross-task generalization claimed without held-out task evaluation.
Split unit unstated; clips from same episode may leak into train and test.
Single runs on small test sets; differences within noise; no intervals.
FVD feature extractor and protocol unspecified.
Table 1 and Table 2 disagree; prose misdescribes Table 1.
5B vs 14B scaling comparison confounded by steps, naming, conditioning.
Human studies under-specified: no agreement stats, rater counts, metric formula, blinding.
Minor: swapped headings, typos, decimals, wrong citation, stray GPT mention, no GPU-hours.
Success rate is visual plausibility; kinematic feasibility untested; robotics claims overstated.
Single embodiment and viewpoint; generating other robot arms not discussed.
Dexterous non-pinch grasps mapped to same gripper abstraction.
Short low-resolution clips; long-horizon and resolution effects not studied.
No breakdown by camera-motion or difficulty level.
Data licensing and commercial API use of source footage not addressed.
Term 'paradoxical in-context learning' unexplained.
'First end-to-end' claim overstated; Human2Robot and AVID not differentiated.
Delta over in-context conditioning small; bidirectional attention not ablated.
Bypassing intermediate representations contradicted by training data built from them.
EPIC metrics measure agreement with renderings, not real robot video.
Positioning against recent human-to-robot translation works thin.
HaMeR lacks bibliography entry.
Teacher-student circularity: Mitty trained on filtered Masquerade renders, compared with raw Masquerade.
Mixed training claims contradict Table 2.
Cross-task generalization claimed without held-out-task test.
Clip split unit unstated.
Numeric inconsistencies across Tables 1-3.
Human-judged success rate lacks agreement statistic; few survey responses; undefined consistency metric.
Small test splits give wide confidence intervals.
Bypass-intermediate-representation claim inconsistent with data pipeline.
Robot-learning claims lack robot-level evidence.
Eq. 4 and DDPM equations mismatch described architecture.
14B naming and step count inconsistent.
Leftover GPT mention in supplement.
Swapped subsection headings.
No analysis of why model works, e.g. attention or conditioning length.
Sole architectural novelty Eq. 4 not ablated.
Mixed-training claims inconsistent with tables.
First-frame claim and SR values inconsistent across tables.
Method underspecified: attention computation, concatenation dimension, training objective unclear.
In-context learning framing over-promises; no actions or novel tasks.
Minor: swapped headings, typos, decimals, unexplained term, GPT mention, 14B naming.

P.summary: Preference comparison unfair due to human filtering.
Synthetic paired data quality and accumulated errors.

Q.summary: Small test sets, no intervals or seeds.
Success metric visual only; robotics claims unsupported.
Bidirectional attention not ablated; small delta.
No analysis of why model works.
